name: Urgent Berlin Java and TypeScript searcher

context.occupation: Software engineer using Java, Spring Boot and TypeScript
context.seniority: Midlevel, approximately four years of experience
context.geography: Berlin; remote employment within Germany also acceptable
context.employment_state: Recently laid off; actively seeking a quick return to employment
constraints: Hybrid in Berlin or remote within Germany
Wants to avoid repeated applications and closed listings
Limited appetite for paid tools before seeing useful coverage
context.company_awareness: Open company list; recognizes some employers but starts with role and location rather than target companies

trigger: After a layoff, the searcher spends a week applying across several boards, opens another apparently suitable listing that has disappeared from the employer site, and realizes one employer has already received an application through a different board.

search_journey.need: See a broad set of local openings immediately.
search_journey.fit_reason: Role and location search fits, but company-first onboarding can slow someone with no shortlist.

search_journey.fit_reason: Technology and location filters help; exact remote conditions still require source inspection.

search_journey.need: Expand beyond Java without changing geography.
search_journey.fit_reason: Technology search can support an adjacent skill search, subject to employer coverage.

search_journey.need: Include international teams and English advertisements.
search_journey.fit_reason: Posting-language filters help find English text; they do not establish workplace language requirements.

searches_run.query: Java Entwickler Jobs Berlin hybrid remote Deutschland
searches_run.observation: Retrieval returned broad StepStone and Indeed category pages, specialist listings and a direct Hubject career posting. Mixed seniority and different remote arrangements appeared. The directly inspected Hubject page describes an intermediate Java role, English workplace language, two Berlin office days weekly, an ASAP start and a two-year contract. These are source statements, not confirmation the vacancy remains unfilled.

searches_run.query: Bewerbungen organisieren doppelte Bewerbungen vermeiden Job Tracker
searches_run.observation: Retrieval included a German discussion about losing track of applications. Direct inspection found requests for Excel templates or apps and replies describing status columns, notes and stored copies of advertisements. This is anecdotal evidence of organization concerns, not evidence of prevalence or demand for automatic duplicate detection.

sources.title: Entwickler/in Java Jobs in Berlin — StepStone
sources.supports: Retrieved category page pairs Java and Berlin with individual listings carrying partial home-office labels; supports the observed role-location landing-page pattern only.

sources.title: Remote Java Developer Jobs in Berlin — Indeed
sources.supports: Retrieved page offers search filters and listings with differing titles and hybrid wording; illustrates that the broad query does not isolate this persona's exact fit.

sources.title: Intermediate Java Developer — Hubject
sources.supports: Direct employer posting specifies four-plus years, English, Berlin hybrid attendance, ASAP start and a two-year contract; shows why details beyond title and remote labels matter.

sources.title: Wie organisiert ihr eure Bewerbungen? — r/arbeitsleben
sources.supports: Directly inspected discussion contains spreadsheet/app requests and manual status, note and advertisement-copy practices. Individual anecdotes only; no representative customer evidence.

best_entry_page.promise: Keep application stages and interview notes together in a free tracker, with a concrete example showing how to review your existing record before applying again.
proof_needed: A working German-language tracker walkthrough with real screenshots
Clear free-feature limits and account requirements
Demonstration of what records users must enter themselves
Explicit explanation of whether externally found roles can be tracked; verify before promising this
A tested path from role/location discovery to selecting covered employers and setting alerts
New indexable landing page; existing account and search pages are noindex

conversion_objections: I need openings now and do not have a prepared list of companies.
Does this cover enough Berlin and German remote employers to justify another account?
How can I tell employer publication time from your detection time?
Can I bring the applications I already sent, or would I maintain two systems?
I already use a spreadsheet; entering everything again could cost more time than I save.
Do German and English filters describe the advertisement or the team's working language?
A paid description-matching feature is secondary until the free search produces relevant roles.

avoid_targeting.query: garantiert aktuelle Java Jobs ohne Ghost Jobs
avoid_targeting.reason: Career-page monitoring cannot guarantee a vacancy is actively being filled.
Urgency is real, but a hiring outcome or timeline cannot be promised.
Tracking can support manual review; automatic cross-board deduplication is unverified.

message_to_founder: Simulation: I need somewhere that gets me to suitable openings quickly, even when I cannot name the companies yet. Let me keep track of what I have already applied for and show me where each opening came from; I would try that before paying for extra matching.
confidence_and_limits: Synthetic persona, not an interview. Fourteen searches are modeled; only the two recorded queries were run. Retrieval observations are not controlled Google rankings, search volumes or conversion evidence. Employer coverage, import support, duplicate handling and freshness semantics require product verification. The strongest opportunity is free German-language application organization connected to role-led discovery; the main mismatch is company selection before an urgent, company-unaware searcher has found options. Proposed acquisition pages do not currently exist.
